# Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

Implementation task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC3).

## Goal

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

## Minimal implementation

- In `GymFormationScene`, add an injectable RNG (`protected rng: () => number = Math.random` plus a `setRng()`/config seam) used for mineral drops.
- Add a single `_spawnMineralKillDrops(entity)` path that calls `resolveMineralKillDrops(...)` and registers the returned minerals in the gym's mineral field.
- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`, `explodeRandom`, RNG seam, mineral field.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — shared helper (from the previous task).

# Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions)

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 6). **Depends on:** child #1 (player tick).

## Summary

`PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` advances the boss inside `tick`, before collisions; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` and *then* advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick(dt)` never advances the boss and bullet timing/ordering differs. `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies()` makes P7 teleport avoid the boss; `GymBoss` does not. `PlayScene._spawnMinions` spawns phase minions; the gym has no equivalent. Move boss advancement onto the shared tick path (via a hook) and align teleport avoidance and minion spawning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — Boss advancement is a shared hook called from `tick`, so a single `tick(dt)` advances the boss in both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` with the same ordering relative to collisions. Verified by a cross-scene test asserting boss bullets appear after the same `tick`.
- [ ] **AC2** — P7 teleport avoids the boss in `GymBoss` as in the game (shared `getAdditionalTeleportBodies` behaviour).
- [ ] **AC3** — Phase-minion spawning matches the game (or is an explicitly documented, producer-approved constrained-feature difference). If mirrored, `GymBoss` uses the shared `planMinionSpawns`.
- [ ] **AC4** — No observable game change; all `PlayScene` boss tests and `GymBoss` tests pass.
- [ ] **AC5** — All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5 and the `GymBoss` docstring.
- [ ] **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — boss-update hook.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_updateBoss` delegates.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — remove `update` override; implement hooks.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts` — reused.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.*boss*` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ4 (epic):** should `GymBoss` spawn phase minions as the game does, or is that a deliberately constrained gym feature? *Recommended: mirror it (behaviour), possibly behind a toggle.*

# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the
  weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level
  readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and
run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and
assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the
GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene:
  round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a
  level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests
  (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart,
  every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling
  real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert
  `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the
  duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not
  duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD;
  otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to
  name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay
  or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record
  any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable
  under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle
  **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an
  optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout;
  keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under
  parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a
  single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way
  to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public
  restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent /
  `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry`
  and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb
  (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace
  `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration
  tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining
  core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals`
  and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the
shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview
when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each
apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and
the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated
  gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?**
  — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title
  and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
  (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?**
  — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is
  identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the
  description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level
  path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7
  behaviour is fully observable?**
  — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the
  default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require
  observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and
  demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the
  threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or
  a gym-local panel?**
  — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` /
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the
  shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the
  established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?**
  — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the
  gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence.
  Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic
  matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal
  relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.
data.title: Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests

## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

# Re-calibrate L4-L5 Generated Campaign Targets After Enemy Bullet-Speed Halving

## Problem statement

Halving every enemy `bulletSpeed` (AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ) lowered each firing archetype's `enemyDifficulty` score by ~0.5–1 point (weight 5/116). The difficulty sequencer's `argmin` now selects degenerate L4–L5 wave compositions — single-enemy firing waves — diverging from hand-tuned targets.

## Users

- **Player** — wants playable, escalating L4–L5 challenge, not trivial single-enemy waves.
- **Game designer** — wants the sequencer to track hand-tuned targets without re-balancing weights.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want L4–L5 campaign waves to present a meaningful, varied challenge, not degenerate single-enemy encounters.
- As a **game designer**, I want the sequencer's generated compositions to stay close to hand-tuned targets without re-tuning enemyDifficulty weights.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Non-degenerate compositions.** No L4–L5 generated wave consists of a single firing enemy. Compositions differ per wave (verified by enemyKey:count).
- **AC2 — Tight band to targets.** Each L4–L5 generated wave's measured `waveDifficulty` is within ±1.0 of its `targetDifficulty`. (Proposed resolution: the original "agreed band" is set to ±1.0, tighter than the existing per-wave CSV tolerance (~2.0), to prevent noticeable drift while allowing valid compositions.)
- **AC3 — No regression to base values.** `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed`, `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`, and every enemy `bulletSpeed` remain at the halved values from AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ.
- **AC4 — Full suite passes.** All tests pass, including new regression tests asserting AC1/AC2 and updated existing regression tests.

## Constraints

- Do not change `FACTOR_RANGES.bulletSpeed`, `FACTOR_WEIGHTS`, or enemy `bulletSpeed` values.
- No divergent copies between gym and game scenes.
- Minimal change: re-derive `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` or enhance `sequenceVariedWaves` — not both.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` (`src/core/configStore.ts`): L4 = [16, 24, 28], L5 = [45, 62].
- `difficulty-curves.csv` has mirrored L4–L5 targets.
- After halving: L4 waves changed from `scoutx18 / diverx18 / tankx18` (measured 22.9/31.3/36.2) to `swarmx1 / tankx1 / phaserx1` (measured 1.8/2.8/3.0).
- L5 w1: `phaserx12+scoutx18` (measured 41.1) → `phaserx12+swarmx1` (measured 29.1).
- Per-wave CSV tolerance is ~2.0 — the shift is within tolerance but composition quality is poor.

## Desired change

Re-derive L4–L5 `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` and `difficulty-curves.csv` rows against **post-halving** `enemyDifficulty` scores so `argmin` selects the same high-quality compositions. If target re-tuning alone is insufficient, enhance `sequenceVariedWaves` to prefer distinct archetypes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — Update `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` for L4/L5.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — Update mirrored L4–L5 targets.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — `sequenceVariedWaves` (if enhanced approach needed).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — New regression: L4–L5 `waveDifficulty` within ±1.0 of target; non-degenerate composition check.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` — Gym-parity regression for AC1/AC2.
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — Read-only: inspect post-halving archetype scores.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep (low).** Re-tuning difficulty weights or reverting bullet-speed halving is documented as out of scope (parent Q3-A).
- **Approach uncertainty (medium).** Re-deriving targets may not fully restore quality if score ordering fundamentally changed; `sequenceVariedWaves` enhancement is the fallback, with more risk.
- **Regression-test churn (low).** Updating targets in `configStore.ts` and `difficulty-curves.csv` will require re-baselining existing pinned tests.
- **Assumption.** Re-deriving targets against post-halving scores is the preferred approach.
- **Assumption.** A ±1.0 difficulty-point tolerance is appropriate.

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent; completed).
- AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K — Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign (completed; prior retuning).
- AH-0MUQ5262M009UFLU — Implement dynamic, varied non-firing opening waves (completed; `DEFAULT_TARGET_OVERRIDES` precedent).
- AH-0MUNU6MGM007CI45 — Launch generated levels from the curve editor (completed; `sequenceVariedWaves` context).
- AH-0MUX3VFUW009M539 — Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks (sibling, non-blocking).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** – Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core scene base class (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)

Raised during intake of AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (field pickups must upgrade temporarily). The producer asked us to *consider creating a second power-up type* to represent consumable temporary grants (P6 Phase Shift charges, P7 Teleport stacks) whose unconsumed grants persist until consumed even after the temporary level window expires.

**discovered-from:AH-0MUX802450085VZZ**

## Goal
Evaluate whether consumable temporary grants should be modelled as a distinct power-up type/category rather than as a level that is temporarily raised. This is an *exploratory* task — no code behaviour change is committed until a design decision is made and accepted.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.

# Demo-mode game-over dwell

## Summary

In demo/attract mode the run currently returns straight to the menu on game
over (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY AC5 — non-scoring). For a full-run capture tail to
show the outcome, the demo must hold on a game-over screen for a configurable
dwell of at least the capture tail before returning to the menu
(parent AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU, AC4).

**User story:** As a viewer of a captured full run, I see the VICTORY/DEFEAT
screen for at least 5 s after the run ends before the demo loops back to the
menu; as a normal player, my game is unchanged and the demo still never writes
to the leaderboard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** In demo mode, game over shows the game-over screen (VICTORY /
  DEFEAT + final score) and holds for `DEMO_GAME_OVER_DWELL_MS` (default
  `>= 5000`, single-source constant) before returning to the menu.
- **AC2:** The demo remains **non-scoring**: it never qualifies for, enters or
  persists a leaderboard score, and never accepts initials.
- **AC3:** Non-demo play is byte-for-byte unchanged: a normal run still
  transitions to the normal interactive `GameOverScene` exactly as before.
- **AC4:** The dwell is configurable and driven by the pure dwell helper from
  the foundation child; an override lets tests run with a short/zero dwell.
- **AC5:** Unit/integration tests cover: dwell duration honoured in demo mode,
  return-to-menu after the dwell, no leaderboard write in demo mode, and
  normal-mode `GameOverScene` unaffected.
- **AC6:** `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

Recommended: start `GameOverScene` from demo `_finishRun` with a demo flag
(`{ won, score, demo: true }`), render the outcome but skip leaderboard
qualification/initials, and schedule the return to `MenuScene` after the dwell.
Alternative (recorded as an OPEN QUESTION): hold an outcome overlay in
`PlayScene` for the dwell. Either way the decision is the pure dwell helper.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — demo `_finishRun` dwell path
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — demo-safe outcome rendering (no scoring)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — tests

## Dependencies

Depends on **Run-end signal, tail and dwell helpers** (dwell decision).

## Deliverables

Configurable, non-scoring demo game-over dwell with tests.
data.title: Demo-mode game-over dwell

# Full-run capture wait, tail and cap

## Summary

Change the **default** demo capture from a fixed-duration clip to a **complete
run**: wait for the end-of-run signal, keep recording a configurable tail
(default `5000` ms), enforce a safety cap, and report the outcome
(parent AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU, AC2/AC3).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I run `npm run capture` once and get a video
of a complete run from Play Game/Watch Demo to 5 s past victory or defeat; if
the run never signals, the tool stops at `--max-duration` and tells me the clip
is incomplete instead of pretending it is a full run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The default (demo) path installs the run-end listener **before the
  game boots** (`page.addInitScript`) and also reads `window.__aiHellRunState`
  as a race fallback, so an early end is not missed.
- **AC2:** `npm run capture` records a complete run from the start of play to
  game over, then continues for `--tail <ms>` (default `5000`) and stops,
  reporting the detected outcome and run length.
- **AC3:** A configurable `--max-duration` cap bounds the recording. When the
  cap is hit with no signal, the tool reports it explicitly and **exits
  non-zero** — a capped clip is never presented as a complete run.
- **AC4:** `--duration` and `--scripted` retain the existing fixed-length
  behaviour; only the default demo path becomes full-run.
- **AC5:** Progress/heartbeat works across an unbounded (capped) recording and
  reports elapsed vs cap.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover arg parsing for `--tail`/`--max-duration`, the
  listener-install plan, and the pure wait/stop loop; the stubbed integration
  assertion lives in the verification child.
- **AC7:** `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace the demo fixed-duration `while` loop with a wait loop driven by the
  pure helpers: poll the signal/flag and the clock, stop at
  `signalTime + tail` or the cap.
- Parse `--tail` / `--max-duration`; keep defaults single-source.
- Update the help text and `--json` payload with outcome/complete/cap fields.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — wait/tail/cap loop, listener install, reporting
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.d.mts` — options/result types
- `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` — heartbeat for an unbounded recording
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — arg/loop tests
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — the signal emitter (dependency)

## Dependencies

Depends on **Run-end signal, tail and dwell helpers** and **Emit dev-gated
end-of-run signal**.

## Deliverables

Full-run default capture with tail, cap, and explicit cap-hit failure.
data.title: Full-run capture wait, tail and cap

## Summary
Instrument the game so a run emits telemetry: per-tick state plus discrete events, tagged with the run seed and schema version. Must cover both human play and the bot, and must not affect gameplay.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Each tick records a compact state vector (player pos/vel/heading, hold/levels, enemies, enemy bullets, drops, minerals, boss) reusing the existing `BotSnapshot` builder where possible.
- AC2: The human/bot input for the tick is recorded alongside the state (the input actually applied).
- AC3: Discrete events are recorded: run start (seed), deaths/hits, pickups, hold-full choice + selection, wave/level transitions, boss phase, run end (win/lose).
- AC4: Recording works when the bot drives and when a human drives, in `PlayScene`; shared-core scenes can opt in.
- AC5: Overhead is bounded and gameplay is unchanged (regression tests); telemetry off = zero records.
- AC6: Unit tests for the state/event serialisation and seed/version tagging.
data.title: Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state and events

## Summary
Dev tooling to record a human session, analyse it offline and replay/ghost it against the bot — the data loop for tuning and evaluating the bot.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A dev command/mode records a human session to JSONL (state + input + events + seed) using the telemetry framework.
- AC2: An offline analysis script produces a report: key-hold duration histogram, input-change cadence, reaction latency proxy, target-choice stats (mineral/power-up/enemy), engagement distances, dodge outcomes, survival/minerals-per-minute.
- AC3: A replay/ghost viewer steps a recording deterministically and overlays human vs bot input/position (same seed).
- AC4: The recorded dataset is versioned and documented so scripts can evolve with the schema.
- AC5: Tests for the analyser (pure stats) and the replay stepping.
- AC6: Docs: how to record, analyse and replay.
data.title: Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling

data.description:
## Summary
Replace the per-frame priority ladder with a **bot framework**: a world model, a registry of goals/behaviours, a committed policy and a content configuration seam. This is the maintainable core that later content and styles plug into.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A `BotBrain`/policy interface that maps a `BotSnapshot` (+ world model + memory) to an input, with an explicit **commitment** mechanism (a selected goal is held until achieved, invalidated, or outranked by a margin for a minimum time).
- AC2: A **goal/behaviour registry**: goals and behaviours register by id; adding one does not require editing the core switch/if-chain.
- AC3: A world-model/predictor layer (positions/velocities, incoming-fire prediction) separated from decision policy, so prediction is testable in isolation.
- AC4: The existing pure `decideBotInput` is preserved behind an adapter (so current tests/gyms keep working) or cleanly superseded with documented parity tests.
- AC5: The framework is deterministic and pure over an injected `dt`/clock; no wall-clock dependence.
- AC6: Unit tests: registry, commitment/hysteresis, deterministic replay of a decision sequence.
- AC7: Docs: framework overview + how goals/behaviours are structured.
data.title: Bot framework core: world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy

data.description:
## Summary
Implement the **competent** structured bot on top of the framework: utility-based goal selection with commitment, behaviour-tree execution (seek → line up → engage/collect → dodge), explicit aim/fire reasoning and predictive dodging. Competent first; style matching comes later.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Goal set covering the operator's order (minerals > power-ups > enemies > asteroids) plus survival, each as a registered goal with a utility/priority and hysteresis.
- AC2: Behaviours: collect (approach + scoop), engage enemy, engage asteroid, evade (predictive path-around, not just direction rejection), reposition/idle.
- AC3: **Aim/fire reasoning**: the bot positions to line up a target while dodging, rather than only aiming by accident of movement.
- AC4: Survival is a hard constraint: never-suicide property tests over sampled snapshots; no wall/enemy/bullet/asteroid collision when a safe alternative exists.
- AC5: Human-like cadence: committed input changes no faster than the human-like toggles; tunables single-sourced.
- AC6: The competent bot completes a representative run (survives/destroys enough) and beats the old ladder on an evaluation metric.
- AC7: Deterministic unit tests per goal/behaviour; integration test on a seeded run.
- AC8: Docs updated (the new decision model).
data.title: Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour tree, predictive dodge/aim

data.description:
## Summary
Make the bot **content-adaptive**: new enemies, power-ups and weapons should be handled via configuration, not core changes, so the bot keeps working as the game grows.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A content config/registry describes, per enemy archetype, threat value, preferred engagement range, aim/lead behaviour and whether it is an asteroid-like hazard.
- AC2: Power-up and weapon definitions declare bot-relevant value/priority (e.g. collection desirability) consumed by the goal scorer.
- AC3: Adding a new enemy/power-up/weapon requires only a config entry (plus its game data) — demonstrated by a test that registers a synthetic content type and the bot handles it.
- AC4: Unknown content degrades gracefully (documented default).
- AC5: Unit tests for the config lookup and the synthetic-content path.
- AC6: Docs: "how to teach the bot about new content".
data.title: Content-adaptive configuration for enemies, power-ups and weapons

## Summary
A reproducible evaluation harness: run the bot (and replay a human recording) on the same seed, produce metrics, A/B two bot versions, and render side-by-side clips. This is how we "re-run the bot production code" after changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A headless runner executes the bot for N ticks/seeds and emits a deterministic report (from telemetry).
- AC2: Same-seed comparison: bot vs human recording, and bot-vs-bot across versions, with metrics (survival time, minerals/min, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed, avoidable hits, input cadence).
- AC3: A/B runner compares two bot configs/versions and reports the difference with confidence (multiple seeds).
- AC4: Optional side-by-side video via the existing capture tooling.
- AC5: Results are reproducible (same seed + config → same report) and stored as artifacts.
- AC6: Tests for the runner/report (pure aggregation) and determinism.
- AC7: Docs: how to run evaluations and interpret the report.
data.title: Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side

## Summary
Later phase: make the bot **match a player's style** using recorded telemetry (parameter fitting and/or behaviour cloning), on top of the competent framework.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A pipeline that extracts style features from human recordings (reaction latency, hold distribution, target preferences, engagement distances, risk appetite).
- AC2: A parameter-fitting path that maps those features onto the structured bot's tunables (preferred first; keeps safety guarantees).
- AC3: (Optional/stretch) A behaviour-cloning policy trained from `(state → input)` pairs, evaluated against the structured bot on the same seeds.
- AC4: Evaluation shows the styled bot is measurably closer to the human recording than the default competent bot, without regressing competence/survival.
- AC5: Docs: how to train/fit and evaluate a style.
- AC6: Tests for the feature extraction (pure).

## Notes
Depends on the recording/analysis tooling and the evaluation harness. Lower priority than competence.

## Summary
Turn on telemetry in **production** for playtesters: an explicit opt-in consent flow, privacy-safe records, batched upload to a remote sink, and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: An in-game consent/opt-in prompt (and a settings toggle) gating production telemetry; default **off**; easy opt-out.
- AC2: A remote sink that batches and uploads records (endpoint configurable), with retry/backoff and no gameplay impact when offline.
- AC3: Records are PII-free and documented; a data-retention/privacy note is included in the docs and (if applicable) the consent screen.
- AC4: A remote-off/no-op path so local dev and offline play are unaffected (tests).
- AC5: A simple way to inspect downloaded telemetry (reuse the analysis tooling from child 4).
- AC6: Tests for consent gating, the uploader's batching/backoff, and the disabled path.
- AC7: Docs: telemetry privacy + how playtester data is stored and used.
data.title: Production telemetry: opt-in consent, privacy, remote sink

# Remove PowerUpType and unify dispatch on PowerUpId

## Summary
Delete the duplicate `PowerUpType` enum and the `PowerUpEntry.type` field so a
single identifier (`PowerUpId`) drives the catalogue, effect dispatch, icon
lookup and the effects registry.

## User story
As a maintainer, I want one identifier per power-up so there is no second
`PowerUpType` union that can drift out of sync with the ID union.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `PowerUpType` no longer exists anywhere under `src/`, and `PowerUpEntry`
   carries no `type` field.
2. Effect dispatch (`src/powerups/effects.ts`), icon/colour lookup
   (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), the effects registry and `getPowerUpById` all key
   off `PowerUpId`; helper signatures (`drawPowerUpIcon`, `drawPowerUpDrop`,
   etc.) updated accordingly.
3. Tests asserting `PowerUpEntry.type` or `PowerUpType` are updated; new or
   updated tests cover the unified dispatch path (catalogue -> effect and
   catalogue -> icon colour for all eight IDs).
4. No duplicate union of power-up identifiers remains; `npm run typecheck`
   and the full test suite pass.

### Parent AC coverage (AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF)

- **Single identifier.** The separate `PowerUpType` enum is removed; effect dispatch, icon lookup, the effects registry and `PowerUpEntry` all key off `PowerUpId` (the redundant per-entry `type` field is dropped). No duplicate union of power-up identifiers remains.

## Minimal implementation
- Remove `PowerUpType` from `src/powerups/types.ts` and the `.type` field from
  catalogue entries and `PowerUpEntry`.
- Switch `effects.ts` dispatch on `entry.id` (values already read as English);
  update the `EffectsRegistry` maps and helper `type` parameters to
  `PowerUpId`.
- Re-key `ICON_COLORS` in `icons.ts` on `PowerUpId`; update switch statements
  and bubble-colour helpers.
- Update tests that construct entries with `type:` or assert `PowerUpType.*`.

## Dependencies
- F2 (name-valued `PowerUpId`) — required before the enum can be deleted.

## Deliverables
- Removed `PowerUpType` enum and `.type` field.
- `PowerUpId`-keyed dispatch/icon/registry code and updated tests.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Remove `PowerUpType`, `PowerUpEntry.type`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Dispatch on `PowerUpId`.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — `ICON_COLORS`/switch keyed on `PowerUpId`.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/icons.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts` — Update fixtures.
- `src/test/powerUpEffectFixtures.ts` — Update effect fixtures.
data.title: Remove PowerUpType and unify dispatch on PowerUpId

# Migrate persisted powerUpWeights to name keys

## Summary
Bump `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` and translate a stored legacy P-keyed
`powerUpWeights` table to the new name keys in `loadRules()`, so customised
drop weights survive the rename (localStorage key `ai-hell-game-rules`).

## User story
As a player with tuned spawn weights, I want my customised drop weights to
survive the upgrade so the rename does not silently reset my configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped from `3` to `4`.
2. `loadRules()` migrates a stored legacy `powerUpWeights` table from the
   `P3`-`P10` keys to the equivalent name keys; unknown or non-numeric keys are
   still ignored; partial tables are still merged over defaults; an
   already-name-keyed config is unchanged.
3. A regression test proves a version-3 config with a customised P-keyed
   weight (for example `P8: 9`) loads under the equivalent name key
   (`extra_life: 9`) with every other rule preserved, and that a version-4
   name-keyed config round-trips unchanged.
4. `saveRules()` persists name-keyed weights with `version: 4`; the existing
   version-1/2 mineral-hold and re-drop migrations are unchanged.

### Parent AC coverage (AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF)

- **Persisted rules migrate.** `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped and `loadRules()` migrates a stored legacy `powerUpWeights` table from the `P3`–`P10` keys to the new name keys, so customised drop weights survive the upgrade. A regression test proves a version-3 config with customised P-keyed weights loads under the equivalent name keys.

## Minimal implementation
- Add a `LEGACY_POWER_UP_ID_BY_CODE` map (`P3` -> `shield`, ... `P10` ->
  `mineral_scoop`) in `src/core/rules.ts`.
- Extend `mergeWeights(stored)` (or add a migration pass keyed on
  `parsed.version < 4`) to translate legacy keys before merging.
- Bump `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 4 and document the migration in the version
  comment.
- Add the regression tests to `src/core/rules.test.ts`.

## Dependencies
- F2 (name-valued `PowerUpId`) — the name keys must exist first.

## Deliverables
- Schema-version bump + legacy weight migration.
- Version-3 regression test and version-4 round-trip test.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `mergeWeights`, migration map.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — v3 migration + v4 round-trip regression tests.
data.title: Migrate persisted powerUpWeights to name keys

# Rename power-ups in docs and docs guards

## Summary
Replace every `P3`-`P10` label in the four in-scope docs with the canonical
power-up names, and update the docs-guard tests and code doc-comments so the
documentation agrees with the source.

## User story
As a designer, I want the docs to name power-ups consistently with the code so
the GDD and source agree.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`,
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and
   `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` contain no remaining `P3`-`P10`
   power-up labels and name power-ups canonically.
2. `src/powerUpLevelingDocs.test.ts`, `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` and any other
   docs-guard tests are updated to the new copy and pass.
3. Power-up label references in code doc-comments (`src/powerups/types.ts`,
   `effects.ts`, `src/core/rules.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`,
   and similar) are updated to the canonical names.

### Parent AC coverage (AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF)

- **Docs renamed.** The GDD, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` name power-ups with the canonical names and contain no remaining `P3`–`P10` label references; the docs-guard tests are updated to match.
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.

## Minimal implementation
- Replace `P3`-`P10` labels with names in the four docs, keeping tables and
  prose readable (for example `P8 Extra Life` -> `Extra Life`).
- Update docs-guard assertions to the new text.
- Sweep code doc-comments for stale P-labels.

## Dependencies
- F2 (canonical names settled).

## Deliverables
- Four renamed docs.
- Updated docs-guard tests and code doc-comments.
- A post-edit grep proving no `P3`-`P10` labels remain in the four docs.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — Replace P-labels with names.
- `src/powerUpLevelingDocs.test.ts`, `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` — Update guards.
- `src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/core/rules.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Doc-comment labels.
data.title: Rename power-ups in docs and docs guards

# Final no-behaviour-change verification

## Summary
Independently verify the completed rename end-to-end: the full test suite, the
gym-to-game equivalence duplicate-body guard, and a clean repo-wide sweep for
legacy literals, confirming this is a pure identifier refactor.

## User story
As a producer, I want a single verification pass proving the rename changed no
gameplay behaviour, so I can approve the parent without re-reading 52 files.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` (full `vitest run`) pass.
2. `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (gym-to-game
   duplicate-body/parity guard) passes.
3. A repo-wide check finds zero `'P3'`-`'P10'` power-up literals under `src/`
   and zero `P3`-`P10` labels in the four in-scope docs.
4. A verification note is recorded on the parent stating the diff contains only
   identifier substitutions (no duration, weight, cap or spawn-order change).

### Parent AC coverage (AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF)

- **No behaviour change.** Gameplay is identical; the full project test suite passes, including the gym↔game duplicate-body/equivalence guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- **Testing/validation.** New or updated unit tests cover the renamed ID catalogue, the removed `PowerUpType` dispatch path and the rules-weight migration.

## Minimal implementation
- Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`; capture the result.
- Run the equivalence guard specifically and capture the result.
- Re-run the F1 guard plus the docs grep.
- Record the verification note as a comment on the parent work item.

## Dependencies
- F2, F3, F4 and F5 — verification runs only after all rename slices land.

## Deliverables
- Verification report comment on AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF with command outputs and
  the no-behaviour-change statement.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/powerups/powerUpIdNaming.test.ts` — Re-run the guard (F1).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Parity guard must pass.
- `package.json` — `typecheck`/`test` scripts.
data.title: Final no-behaviour-change verification
